name: base16
short_description: Human-readable binary encoding with a character set designed to minimize transcription errors.
long_description: Base16 is a hexadecimal-like encoding system that uses a carefully chosen alphabet (A, B, C, D, E, G, H, K, P, R, S, T, W, X, Y, Z) instead of standard hex characters. It's designed to minimize user frustration and transcription errors when handling high-entropy data like voucher codes, confirmation codes, and verification tokens. The project includes automatic error-correction that maps similar-looking invalid characters to correct base16 characters based on 1983 research on human transcription patterns. It provides both a Python library API and command-line interface for encoding, decoding, and generating random base16 strings.

modules.description: Core encoding/decoding logic with character mapping tables and fuzzy matching for similar-looking characters.
Package initialization that exports public API functions: encode, decode, random, encode_hex, decode_hex.
Command-line interface with argument parsing for encode, decode, random operations, and piped input/output support.
Comprehensive test suite covering encoding/decoding, fuzzy mode, filtering, hex operations, random generation, and performance benchmarks.
